notes.title: CUSTOM BATTLES CONTEST
notes.content:
[h1]Submission ends on the 4th of March at 12.00 CET.[/h1]
No custom battles after 12:00 CET will be accepted!

[h2]What are custom battles?[/h2]
Players are able to create their own custom battles for Everhood.
The battles are created inside Unity

Here is an example:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lk6Cxf-SBWo&t=1s

There are tons more in 
CustomBattles/ #library-of-battles in [url=https://discord.gg/qEPhjQj]Discord[/url]

[h2]Prices:[/h2]
[list]
[*] 1st price - T-shirt, pin, 200 USD (Paypal) + a copy of Everhood
[*] 2nd price - T-shirt, pin, and 50 USD (Paypal) + a copy of Everhood
[*] 3rd price - T-shirt and pin + a copy of Everhood
[*] 4th price - T-shirt + a copy of Everhood
[*] 5th price - T-shirt + a copy of Everhood
[/list]

All participants will have a unique discord role:
Year1-Gnome

Money will be sent using Paypal! 
(if not possible we can donate the money from a selection we’ll provide!)

Anyone can join!
(moderators and custom battle moderators) All will be judged equally!

[h2]Rules[/h2]
[list]
[*] No previously published custom battles.
[*] No custom battles after 4th march 12:00 CET will be accepted!
[*] Collaborate with any amount of people per battle(you share the price then!)
[*] You can submit a maximum of 5 battles. (but you can only win one prize)
[*] Use any music you like!
[*] Have fun!
[/list]

[h2]Important Info[/h2]
Submit your custom battle inside the Everhood discord by simply dropping it in CustomBattle-Year1Contest/#Submission along with a thumbnail and a short description 
Any other comments in the submission channel will be deleted!
Make sure to test your submission!
 If it is broken we won’t reach out and contact you. We will be forced to disqualify the submission!

[h2]Some other info:[/h2]
If you want to share your progress on Twitter use the hashtag  #Everhood1YearBattleContest.
Judges(Chris & Jordi) will be guided by / take into consideration:

Creativity - How unique the battle is compared to others!
Visuals - Compositions, contrast and/or how clear things are!
Level Design - Does the level design feel like it is complementary to the music?
Technical expertise - What sort of advanced technical things are going on here?
Music-taste - Does the song evoke feelings?
Bonus points if you create your own music!* (make sure to mention it!)

[h2]How to get started:[/h2]
1. Own a copy of Everhood for PC
2. All resources and tutorials are located in #resources on how to get started!
3. If you have any questions feel free to ask them in #Workshop 

[h2]Announcement of winner: [/h2]
Depends mainly on the amount of custom battles!
Hopefully around 16th March!

[i](note: the [url=https://discord.gg/qEPhjQj]discord [/url]information will always be the most accurate)[/i]

notes.title: Replay Battles feature + Localization Update
notes.content:
[h1]Replay Battle feature[/h1]

We are thrilled to announce the highly requested replay battles feature!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/10e000c998b5d044de6987464869e0a3d056518b.gif[/img]

After the player finishes the game(genocide ending) they can access replay battles in the main menu which is accompanied with a unique score system and online leaderboards!

Players will have access to all battles except some special encounters such as incinerators and quantum battles (which is not really a battle!) but we are happy to announce that the medallion sword battles and the tennis battles are included!

We have two rating systems the star system and the online leaderboard score system.

[h2]The star system[/h2]
This is based on how much damage the player received.
[list]
[*] 1 star = 10+ damage
[*] 2 stars = 5+ damage
[*] 3 stars = 3+ damage
[*] 4 stars = 1+ damage
[*] 5 stars = no damage
[/list]
[h2]The online leaderboard score system
[/h2]Earn points while playing a battle.
Points: 
[list]
[*] Sidestep or jump rolling to avoid a projectile: 75 points.
[*] Jump over a projectile: 50 points.
[*] Taking damage = -500 points.
[/list]
[b]During killmode
[/b][list]
[*] Absorb small energy = 50 points.
[*] Absorb tall energy = 100 points.
[*] Damaging enemy = 500 points.
[*] Destroy a small energy = 50 points.
[*] Destroy a tall energy = 100 points.
[/list]

[b]After battle[/b]
Upon victory, the player receives a time bonus that is calculated depending on duration of the song and then adds all points gathered during the battle and finally multiplies with the chosen difficulty:
[list]
[*] Story mode = x1
[*] Easy =  x5
[*] Normal = x10
[*] Hard = x25
[*] Expert = x50
[*] Insane = x100
[/list]

Other worthy notes:

The leaderboard will reset every month.
No-hit achivements can be obtained in Replay Battles feature.
As of now, this update is only for PC but in the future, we hope to get it into the Nintendo switch!
The score system is not available in the normal playthrough only accessible in the replay battle.

Also thank you to Alessandro Cominu from Subvert Games for the backend support of the online leaderboard!


[h1]Localization efforts[/h1]

Early in development people in our discord channel recommended that we should open up for the game to be translated.

We are happy to say that we now support:
[b]Italian, German, Russian, Spanish, Euskara, French, Japanese, Chinese, Traditional Chinese,[/b] and of course[b] English.[/b]
Here are a few images of the different localizations in no particular order!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/64989932d5d2f498c6858782a72196a711439bf1.png[/img]

notes.title: Photosensitivity tests - Cambridge Research Systems
notes.content:
[h1]Image sensitivity option[/h1]

Since its launch date, Everhood has always had Image sensitivity available for players.

Here is two images from the same battle with image sensitivity option on/off

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/fbb0b1bf150f5f7a475f6b5c965b207acbfbdd5b.png[/img]
Gif: [url=https://i.imgur.com/Dbqwvrw.gifv]https://i.imgur.com/Dbqwvrw.gifv[/url]

The accessibility option is available inside Everhood game settings window, in the accessibility tab.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/dd418449ca2cb294423b0eeb2b15956c4023e9fb.png[/img]

As you can guess the option has been available for quite some time for players, but we weren't sure where our game stood out in terms of epilepsy / seizure-prone triggers; some clear metrics/data was needed.

[h1]Harding FPA - Cambridge Research Systems
[/h1]

We ended up using Harding FPA software to analyze photosensitivity from Cambridge research systems ([url=https://www.hardingfpa.com/]https://www.hardingfpa.com/[/url]) which have been used for many video games and television programs to spot photosensitivity types of issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/16c4aa2cd8583924b614fac97b02852eb4a09bf6.png[/img]

After some weeks of testing we are confident to say that:

Everhood is at a very low risk of being seizure prone according to the data collected, even with Image sensitivity OFF.  (we can't control how close you are to screen or playing in an unlit room etc)
Still, our Image sensitivity option suffered some tweaks here and there in order to improve it because we think it remains as an useful option for players who are prone to get headaches.

[h1]More in-depth examples
[/h1]

When doing some tests , we had one case where the system failed Everhood but only briefly which was during the late stage of the Incinerator and it was when the incinerator was flashing several times in this square formation without the image sensitivity turned on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/d6914308d1a9bd2293acecfd051343f3350aa394.png[/img]

This has now been adjusted in the latest release, Only 0.8-2.5% of all the players ever reached this area according to our data.

So the gnome battle, did it pass the seizure test?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/50d762b28d2a05e70de106c1e14eaecc22dfe211.png[/img]
Gif: [url=https://imgur.com/OPj5YJG]https://imgur.com/OPj5YJG[/url]

In fact, yes it did.
We were quite surprised by this and contacted the photosensitivity software makers and sent the footage to Cambridge Research Systems scientist to analyze as we suspected we might have missed something.

They confirmed that our findings were correct shared some in-depth explanations why:

Cambridge Research Systems Ltd : [i]“The video(battle) passed the flash and pattern guidelines with ease, registering occasional spatial activity which is insufficient to generate the blue spatial pattern trace (see the Advanced Information tab in the attached screenshot).

In this case, the radial pattern is low contrast with a pixelated appearance so this is not sufficiently regular to pose a problem.

In addition, it is rotating so this would only have the potential to generate a spatial pattern warning and would have to remain stationary for more than 0.5 seconds to generate a spatial pattern failure.”[/i]

We also took some time experimenting with other footage to test the system such as the Undertale Flowey boss which we assume is the most visually intense battle in Undertale.
The entire battle only got a “cautious warning”.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/62ec719ad574d162b76aa59dbabc4e9cbea31995.png[/img]

The intro of Enter The Void was very seizure-prone though just to give an example.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/50b6b1291a5bbccbf0f5b3004770eff99eda6c9c.png[/img]
Video: [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wNtxgxYY7sI]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wNtxgxYY7sI[/url] (warning this is REALLY REALLY EYE BLEEDING, but cool)
(No meant to discourage Enter The Void, I thought I'd just share the data for fun!)

[h1]TLDR:[/h1]

[list]
[*] Everhood passed Harding FPA - Cambridge Research Systems tests (photosensitivity  software) meaning the game is not seizure-prone.

[*] Everhood has an Image Sensitivity option in order to reduce game light effects if you're still a bit sensitive to funky colors AND it has been improved thanks to the useful data gathered by the Harding FPA photosensitivity software.
[/list]

Have a great day!

[list]
[*] A lot of proofreading.
[*] Disabled movement when talking to midnight town door.
[*] New incinerator part 2 background as previous background had poor performance on a few computers.
[*] Credits updated.
[*] Added delay to interaction inputs when scene load to avoid any weird interaction while the scene is not finished loading.
[*] Added missing translated sentences.
[*] Fixed NG+ flag was very inconsistent.
[*] Optimized topdown songs and sound memory sizes.
[*] Removed more visual stuff when Photosensivity ON
[*] Fixed setting difficulty selector doesn’t work well with Insane difficulty
[*] Fixed Last projectiles of Purple Mage battle were not jumpable
[*] Fixed some topdown walls collision, I challenge you to go out of the map
[*] Now the game doesn’t break if the game save is corrupt

notes.title: What has happened update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/21cacb287945596ff47201e2819996deca41bcf6.png[/img]
Environment artwork by Mimi

Past devlogs we have been doing announcing updates after the steam release  rather than doing more personal devlogs

One important highlight is that one of our discord members PhilipL made a wiki for Everhood
https://everhood.fandom.com/wiki/Everhood_Wiki

I took sometime to go through our previous devlogs and read what we have written and I personally found the ones where I have written down my thoughts at the time being the one interesting or if we hit an important milestone

So I thought I would do it again!

After releasing the new demo on steam we have really gained a lot of new eyes and people in the discord. I told our discord moderator BartTheBart that he could expect an influx of people coming in but couldn’t have expected it would grow up to 900discord members and there is usually some sort of daily discussion, theories, art or wiki’s showing up which really motivates us

Reading through everything has surely impacted the development and brought up discussion between me and Jordi and we are very thankful to see these interactions and expectations of the game which makes us more confident, even if it is potentially only a small “loud” portion.

Two weeks ago we had a blind stream and afterward a Q&A. Unfortunately, none of us recorded it but it was a nice unfiltered casual experience

We have been doing a lot of playtests before and are currently right now undergoing a big haul of the last content making as we are aiming for a content-lockdown at the end of July and after that focusing on just making sure that what we got is as bugfree as possible.

A content-lockdown aka content freeze is essential that we don’t produce more content but just making sure game is playable

We decide to do an early content-lockdown so we can catch as many bugs as possible as our testing capabilities are low because most of the testing is done by me and Jordi and then we monitor playtesters and try to have as stable builds as possible

We are aiming to send out the game to more playtesters that are unmonitored as we are confident the gameplay value is good, we just need to find all the edges cases where the game breaks if players do things in strange-sequences.

Healthwise I am(Chris) not 100% recovered since last year in May, I am not sure when I will feel better, I will most likely have to take a break somewhere after development (one week, one month, idunno!), I am still doing ten times better than what I did before and I only work when I am feeling good, it’s just somedays or sometimes I ain’t working as I used to.
Jordi is chugging along as usual and has been working like a damn trooper making sure that the game takes that extra step to become a great experience for everyone.

I would love to write some awesome anecdotes about how certain development endeavors have worked out but without context, it would be pointless, I know we are going to write some posts about it at some point. All I can say right now is that it is usually me who is setting up encounters and making the battles while Jordi makes sure everything is running smoothly and I have sufficient tools to make it, but once something gets too technical Jordi usually has to take it the entire way and I provide feedback as a playtester and give him art assets while he has full creative control.

I just want to say that he had just created something really cool that is going to be awesome to see if YouTubers or streamers play

Overall I feel that our workload is moderate and we will be able to deliver something not good, but great. We are on a constant lookout for nasty bugs and I hope we get some of them during our bigger upcoming playtesting sessions

Just want to highlight that CakeLullabies and Metroidhat​ who made a Red plushie which is awesome
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/99d1bb3a5b934ca616178256cef0a8a9671e1ff5.jpg[/img]

Also, like to point out that we have three new moderators for the discord channel
PhilipL, Cakelullabies, and Faust!

Stuff will be as usual in the channel but good to have it


Have a great one!

notes.title: Main gameplay update
notes.content:
[h1]Smear effect for player movement
[/h1]
First of all we added a smear effect on when Red is moving and jumping! Thanks to our discord member Kirby and PhilipL for the suggestion of adding that effect It really looks and feels better and fits well for the character!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/ef26915c5d6c402b6e0bb1446b914337ece623c0.gif[/img]


[h1]Possible new health UI
[/h1]
After many playtesting sessions we have gotten feedback about the health system being sub-par visually. It was mainly ugly and we have removed it from the old trailer because of this reason as well as it’s distracting.

In some cases we noticed players were surprised as they didn’t understand why they died when taken damage when the gameplay got extra hectic.

So our way to fix this is by putting health on the main character

We did a lot of concepts of different health

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/d70c0dda25cf40fa17763e481336f6a69d4d20e8.png[/img]
In the end, we decided with this approach:

A- HealthBar

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/114f192797b975feb992f6948a6ff618e7113130.gif[/img]
One important factor was to get rid of the bars as it will potentially unlock more design flexibility of some projectiles adding less damage and we can keep that number a bit hidden if needed, it could be a useful tool if needed. Previously we pretty much looked at rock bands and copied. Rockband’s solution is okay and very clear once you know what to look for but doesn’t feel entirely natural for non-gamers

We understand some players might feel it was better before, mainly that it was clearer before but we think the new design will feel more coherent in the world, makes it more clear for new players, and also potentially helps us for balancing issues!

We also had some other health user interface candidate :

B- Reverse sidebar
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/7da6aac3a375afcfb23a28e9d28534eb35a102c9.gif[/img]

C- Normal
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37126515/775379a5d164fd0507ea453c863650139b143b96.gif[/img]

notes.title: Playtesting!
notes.content:
We just had our first playtest after the demo release. 

It took some time and a lot of discussions embarked during the testing.

There is certainly potential here but we still need to fix and adjust stuff


We won’t make the perfect game but it sure will be something you will enjoy and share with your friends this crazy adventure.


[h2]A WEEK LATER[/h2]

I keep looking for something that will potentially break the entire thing but so far haven’t found anything that hasn’t been able to fix.

Tomorrow we will have another internal playtest and try to go through the entire game. This will be an entire new playtester as previously we have had returning playtesters so I am excited to see how this one goes. Usually, our playtesting is done on-location but this one will be through private streaming due to coronavirus.

As we have set up a hard deadline and a promise that the game will be done Q4(October-December) 2020 I am always (very in lack of better words) vigilant of not adding new features or behaviors, we have already done some of it known as feature-creeping but we have setup dates of content-lockdown as no more adjustments of features after a specific date to help us shipping the game.

Hopefully, this playtest will show good results even if we have some buffer time before release. But we really want to have more life-quality features added such as more settings controls or flesh out more environmental parts of the game as they tend to be things we have prioritized lower in the production.


[h2]DAY AFTER PLAYTEST[/h2]

Like usual after a playtest session I am completely exhausted from being focused all day. We encountered a few game-breaking bugs but not serious cases as they are all easy to fix.

The testers gave us a lot of useful info and we are in a good space but not in a shipping state yet. We are gonna take some time to adjust the problems which will probably be fixed fast but then also polish the bits that we are not so proud of. In a few weeks, we will do additional internal testing.

Overall I think the test went superbly, we know some pain points that still need to be addressed, some that are hard and some that just require a cup of coffee which are not a priority to adjust.
